\section[brigar]{brigar — to quarrel, to fight}

\label{lesson:PT-C497-brigar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for to stroke, then the Portuguese for to spoil.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: brigar}
\textbf{brigar} — \textquotedblleft{}to quarrel, to fight\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Os irmãos brigam por tudo.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The brothers fight over everything.}
\end{quote}

Very common in Brazil; in Portugal \emph{zangar-se} and \emph{discutir} are frequent too.

\begin{cousinweb}
EtymDB traces \emph{brigar} to Gothic \emph{brikan} \textquotedblleft{}to break\textquotedblright{}; other accounts suggest other sources, so the origin is not fully settled.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{brigar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{brigar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{brigar}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for to stroke, then the Portuguese for to spoil, then say \emph{brigar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does brigar mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To quarrel, to fight\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[separar]{separar — to separate; to split up (separar-se)}

\label{lesson:PT-C497-separar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for to spoil, then the Portuguese for to quarrel.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: separar}
\textbf{separar} — \textquotedblleft{}to separate; to split up (separar-se)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Os pais dele separaram-se no ano passado.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{His parents split up last year.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Separar o lixo} — to sort the rubbish.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{separar} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{sēparāre} \textquotedblleft{}to separate\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), built on \emph{sē-} \textquotedblleft{}apart\textquotedblright{} and \emph{parāre} \textquotedblleft{}to prepare\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{separar}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for to spoil, then the Portuguese for to quarrel, then say \emph{separar} again

\section[trair]{trair — to betray; to cheat on}

\label{lesson:PT-C497-trair}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for to quarrel, then the Portuguese for to separate.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: trair}
\textbf{trair} — \textquotedblleft{}to betray; to cheat on\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Ele traiu a confiança dos amigos.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{He betrayed his friends' trust.}
\end{quote}

Present: \emph{traio}, \emph{trais}, \emph{trai}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{trair} is inherited, through Old Portuguese \emph{traer}, from Latin \emph{trādere} \textquotedblleft{}to hand over, to betray\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[a traição]{a traição — betrayal}

\label{lesson:PT-C497-traicao}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for to separate, then the Portuguese for to betray.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a traição}
\textbf{a traição} — \textquotedblleft{}betrayal\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Para ela, a mentira foi uma traição.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{For her, the lie was a betrayal.}
\end{quote}

Built like \emph{trair} on Latin \emph{trādere}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{traição} is inherited, through Old Portuguese \emph{traiçon}, from Latin \emph{trāditiōnem} \textquotedblleft{}a handing over\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[reconciliar]{reconciliar — to reconcile; to make up (reconciliar-se)}

\label{lesson:PT-C497-reconciliar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for to betray, then the Portuguese for betrayal.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: reconciliar}
\textbf{reconciliar} — \textquotedblleft{}to reconcile; to make up (reconciliar-se)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Depois de anos sem se falarem, os dois irmãos reconciliaram-se.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{After years of not speaking, the two brothers made up.}
\end{quote}

Everyday Portugal also says \emph{fazer as pazes}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{reconciliar} comes from Latin \emph{reconciliāre} \textquotedblleft{}to bring together again\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
